cases.sentence: О той партии пленных, в которой был Пьер, во время всего своего движения от Москвы, не было от ___ никакого нового распоряжения.
cases.explain: «французского начальства» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: During the whole of their march from Moscow no fresh orders had been issued by the French authorities concerning the party of prisoners among whom was Pierre. On the twenty-second of October that party was no longer with the same troops and baggage trains with which it had left Moscow. Half the wagons laden with hardtack that had traveled the first stages with them had been captured by Cossacks, the other half had gone on ahead. Not one of those dismounted cavalrymen who had marched in front of the prisoners was left; they had all disappeared. The artillery the prisoners had seen in front of them during the first days was now replaced by Marshal Junot’s enormous baggage train, convoyed by Westphalians. Behind the prisoners came a cavalry baggage train.

cases.sentence: Те признаки беспорядка, которые заметил Пьер на ___ из Москвы, теперь дошли до последней степени.
cases.explain: «первом привале» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: From Vyázma onwards the French army, which had till then moved in three columns, went on as a single group. The symptoms of disorder that Pierre had noticed at their first halting place after leaving Moscow had now reached the utmost limit.

cases.sentence: Дорога, по которой они шли, с обеих сторон была уложена мертвыми лошадьми; ___, отсталые от разных команд, беспрестанно переменяясь, то присоединялись, то опять отставали от шедшей колонны.
cases.explain: «оборванные люди» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The road along which they moved was bordered on both sides by dead horses; ragged men who had fallen behind from various regiments continually changed about, now joining the moving column, now again lagging behind it.

cases.sentence: Несколько раз во время похода бывали ___, и солдаты конвоя поднимали ружья, стреляли и бежали стремглав, давя друг друга, но потом опять собирались и бранили друг друга за напрасный страх.
cases.explain: «фальшивые тревоги» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Several times during the march false alarms had been given and the soldiers of the escort had raised their muskets, fired, and run headlong, crushing one another, but had afterwards reassembled and abused each other for their causeless panic.

cases.sentence: Эти три сборища, шедшие вместе — ___, депо пленных и обоз Жюно, — всё еще составляли что-то отдельное и цельное, хотя и то, и другое, и третье быстро таяло.
cases.explain: «кавалерийское депо» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: These three groups traveling together—the cavalry stores, the convoy of prisoners, and Junot’s baggage train—still constituted a separate and united whole, though each of the groups was rapidly melting away.

cases.sentence: Три повозки были разграблены набежавшими ___ из корпуса Даву.
cases.explain: «отсталыми солдатами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Of the artillery baggage train which had consisted of a hundred and twenty wagons, not more than sixty now remained; the rest had been captured or left behind. Some of Junot’s wagons also had been captured or abandoned. Three wagons had been raided and robbed by stragglers from Davout’s corps. From the talk of the Germans Pierre learned that a larger guard had been allotted to that baggage train than to the prisoners, and that one of their comrades, a German soldier, had been shot by the marshal’s own order because a silver spoon belonging to the marshal had been found in his possession.

cases.sentence: Пленные еще более, чем седла ___ и чем обоз Жюно, тяготили конвоирующих солдат.
cases.explain: «кавалерийского депо» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The group of prisoners had melted away most of all. Of the three hundred and thirty men who had set out from Moscow fewer than a hundred now remained. The prisoners were more burdensome to the escort than even the cavalry saddles or Junot’s baggage. They understood that the saddles and Junot’s spoon might be of some use, but that cold and hungry soldiers should have to stand and guard equally cold and hungry Russians who froze and lagged behind on the road (in which case the order was to shoot them) was not merely incomprehensible but revolting. And the escort, as if afraid, in the grievous condition they themselves were in, of giving way to the pity they felt for the prisoners and so rendering their own plight still worse, treated them with particular moroseness and severity.

cases.sentence: С Каратаевым, на ___ выхода из Москвы, сделалась та лихорадка, в которой он лежал в Московском гошпитале, и, по мере того как Каратаев ослабевал, Пьер отдалялся от него.
cases.explain: «третий день» — after the preposition «по», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: On the third day after leaving Moscow Karatáev again fell ill with the fever he had suffered from in the hospital in Moscow, and as he grew gradually weaker Pierre kept away from him. Pierre did not know why, but since Karatáev had begun to grow weaker it had cost him an effort to go near him. When he did so and heard the subdued moaning with which Karatáev generally lay down at the halting places, and when he smelled the odor emanating from him which was now stronger than before, Pierre moved farther away and did not think about him.

cases.sentence: Он не видал и не слыхал, как пристреливали ___, хотя более сотни из них уже погибли таким образом.
cases.explain: «отсталых пленных» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: He did not see and did not hear how they shot the prisoners who lagged behind, though more than a hundred perished in that way. He did not think of Karatáev who grew weaker every day and evidently would soon have to share that fate. Still less did Pierre think about himself. The harder his position became and the more terrible the future, the more independent of that position in which he found himself were the joyful and comforting thoughts, memories, and imaginings that came to him.
